notes:
Spec asserts ready → working → ready for a tool-less turn that ends in assistant text. COPILOT'S END SIGNAL IS A SEPARATE EVENT: assistant.message carries the reply text (parser.go parseAssistantMessage → EventType assistant_message, AssistantText via tailer.TruncateAssistantText) and deliberately NEVER settles the turn; the explicit assistant.turn_end boundary (with turnId) maps to turn_done, which makes SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone true (metrics.go:542) and fires classifier rule 2b working → ready. That is strictly safer than an inference-based end signal — no quiet-tail heuristic, no stop_reason allow-list a new enum value could fall out of. A turn may contain several assistant.message events before its single assistant.turn_end, so the terminal text is the LAST one; the recipe elicits a single short declarative reply. PRESESSION SHAPE (provisional, from code): copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row (1s poll) before the fswatcher sees any transcript; the real session then arrives under a DIFFERENT id. Birth is modeled as two phases and every post-birth phase anchors to the REAL session (codex/mistral-vibe template). turn_end_terminal anchors to turn_start (not session_birth) so the matcher picks the post-turn ready rather than the birth ready. Overlaps intentionally with basic-turn (2.1): that cell asserts the lifecycle including pid_bind, this one asserts only the end-signal arc plus the no-tool-call invariant. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map (session.usage_checkpoint carries no token counts — only shutdown does). model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn, so an exact match would be nondeterministic.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-03: the real session is born directly into `working`, not `ready`. copilot writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so at discovery the file ALREADY holds the open turn; since commit 3cde4f8d ("fix(detector): classify every new session against its own metrics, not just children") buildNewSessionState classifies that birth against its own metrics instead of hard-coding StateReady. Recording 2026-08-03-17-50-15 shows state_transition(reason="new session created") landing new_state=working on the real session. The transient proc-<PID> row is still born ready and remains the presession_birth anchor. The pre-fix spec asserted a ready birth followed by a separate ready→working; that shape was the bug the fix removed, so session_birth and turn_start are now ONE phase.
source: .specs/agent-scenarios.md → Feature: Turn end via terminal text

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
The real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, and is born DIRECTLY into working because the file already holds the open turn
assistant.turn_end closes the tool-less text turn → ready (turn_done → IsAgentDone → classifier rule 2b); the session never entered waiting and never opened a tool call
